query: Package Vikunja (https://vikunja.io, self-hosted to-do app) for our Umbrel app store. Use PostgreSQL, not SQLite.
expected_behavior: Creates yakitori-vikunja/ with umbrel-app.yml, docker-compose.yml, exports.sh and data/<dir>/.gitkeep for every bind-mount source
id is yakitori-vikunja, version is a quoted string matching the latest stable upstream release, icon and gallery are absolute https URLs pinned to a tag or SHA
Picks a manifest port that check.sh reports as free in both this store and the official store
Every image (vikunja and postgres) is tag@sha256 obtained from scripts/resolve-image.mjs and covers linux/amd64 and linux/arm64
The database host is yakitori-vikunja_db_1 (or <id>_<service>_1), never a bare service name
Postgres password and JWT secret come from derive_entropy with distinct labels in exports.sh; no literal secrets in compose
Postgres has a TCP pg_isready healthcheck with start_period and the app waits with condition: service_healthy; no user: on the postgres service
storage.dataRoot: data is declared and all durable state is under ${APP_DATA_DIR}/data/
Public URL is derived from DEVICE_DOMAIN_NAME and ${APP_PROXY_PORT:-<port>} and exposed as a manifest environment override
Runs scripts/check.sh yakitori-vikunja --check-images and reaches zero errors before declaring done
States clearly whether on-device testing was done; does not claim the app works from lint alone

query: In yakitori-daily-hub the MCP whitelist /mcp/* exposes Next.js server actions. Restrict it to exactly /mcp and ship the fix.
expected_behavior: Changes PROXY_AUTH_WHITELIST to the exact path(s) needed and explains why /mcp/* was dangerous
Bumps version (e.g. 0.2.7 -> 0.2.7-umbrel.1) because installed devices only receive compose changes on a version change
Rewrites releaseNotes for upgrading users and mentions the security fix
Runs scripts/check.sh yakitori-daily-hub --base origin/master and gets no update.version_not_bumped error
Verifies (or asks to verify on a device) that /mcp works without the Umbrel cookie and that /mcp/anything now redirects to Umbrel login

query: Update yakitori-chartbrew to the latest upstream release.
expected_behavior: Reads upstream release notes for every version between the packaged one and the target, not only the latest
Re-pins every changed image with scripts/resolve-image.mjs and keeps the Postgres major version unchanged

Notices that web/server.cjs is bind-mounted from a package file outside the update whitelist (package.frozen_mount) and moves it inline into compose or a top-level .template, or flags it explicitly to the user
Keeps service names, environment names and derive_entropy labels unchanged
Updates version and releaseNotes, runs check.sh with --base origin/master, and describes the update-path test (install shipped version, create data, update, verify)

query: Review yakitori-doop for anything that could break on users' devices.
expected_behavior: Runs scripts/check.sh yakitori-doop --check-images
Reports the bare @db:5432 hostname as a cross-app collision risk and gives the <id>_db_1 fix
Reports Postgres data and secrets outside data/ despite storage.dataRoot, and that hook-generated secrets are not reproducible
Reports the amd64-only wrapper image
Audits PROXY_AUTH_WHITELIST (/api/auth/*, /.well-known/*) for sign-up or unauthenticated routes
Proposes fixes that are update-safe for existing installs (migration hook for moved data, version bump), not only for fresh installs

query: Our app needs a 32-byte base64 encryption key and an https base URL. Write the exports.sh.
expected_behavior: Derives the key with derive_entropy "${app_entropy_identifier}-<purpose>" and converts the 64 hex chars to 32 raw bytes before base64
Uses ${APP_PROXY_PORT:-<manifest port>} and ${DEVICE_DOMAIN_NAME:-umbrel.local}, never bare $APP_PROXY_PORT or a hardcoded umbrel.local
No shebang, no set/exit/cd, no openssl rand; helper variables are unset at the end
Mentions that the label must never change after release because the key encrypts stored data
